title: Ireland – Construction work for bridges and tunnels, shafts and subways – Global PIN for the MetroLink programme related to: • Programme Delivery Partner (PDP) Contract. • M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • M500 Contract (DBFOM).
description: MetroLink will provide a high speed, high capacity, high frequency, modern and efficient public transport service for passengers travelling along the Swords/Airport to City Centre corridor in Dublin, which will be capable of integration with other modes of public transport. Further information on MetroLink is available at www.metrolink.ie MetroLink will be procured under a series of public works and services contracts: Programme Delivery Partner (“PDP”) Contract: The PDP Contract shall support Transport Infrastructure Ireland (“TII”) through providing capability and capacity to support the TII organisational structure in post-contract, construction and delivery (including contract management functions such as fulfilling role of “Project Manager” and “Supervisor” under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and performance of the statutory function of Project Supervisor Construction Stage under the M401/M402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract). M401/402 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts: Two NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) contracts will be let for the civil engineering and infrastructure works including track alignment preparation, stations and structures including bridges and tunnels. Further detail on the scope of the two M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts is as envisaged below: 1. Southern Section M401 – Charlemont to Northwood: • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Below ground station excavations at Charlemont, St Stephen’s Green, Tara, O’Connell, Mater, Glasnevin, Griffith Park, Collins Avenue, Ballymun, Northwood up to 35m deep including shell and core structures. 2. Northern Section M402 - Northwood to Estuary: • M50 viaduct, surface route (retained cut, cut and cover) and at-grade sections; • Broadmeadow river viaduct; • Estuary Station Park and Ride Facility (bulk earthworks and site preparation); • Preparation of the Dardistown Depot site and access road; • Bored tunnels and portals, evacuation / intervention shafts; and • Stations excavations and associated logistics including Dardistown, Dublin Airport, Fosterstown, Swords Central, Seatown and Estuary. M500 Contract An availability-based design, build, finance, operate and maintain (“DBFOM”) contract to appoint a project company (“M500 Contractor”) who will carry out design and construction, raise finance in respect of such construction, and subsequently provide the integrated operation and maintenance of the public passenger transport service. The M500 Contractor will be responsible for the design, manufacture, supply and installation of the metro rolling stock, signalling system (at Grade of Operation 4 – an automated railway), a railway depot and maintenance facility, metro control centre building(s) together with the installation of all line-wide trackwork, overhead contact system, power and communication systems, mechanical and electrical systems including tunnel and station ventilation, people movement systems and the fit out and finishes in sixteen stations plus urban realm works. The M500 Contractor will be required to procure financing in respect of the abovementioned works, and following completion of the works, the M500 Contractor will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the MetroLink system as a whole. TII proposes to award an Early Services Agreement to the preferred tenderer for the M500 Contract, pursuant to which the preferred tenderer will be required to provide early services related to, inter alia, railway systems integration prior to financial close. In advance of the award of the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts and the M500 Contract, TII intends to award a series of enabling works framework agreements (the “M100 Contracts”) and a DPS purchasing system to deliver enabling works to include the removal and/or relocation of existing utilities, archaeology, heritage items (for storage/replacement) and buildings from site and undertaking other monitoring and survey activities. Separate Periodic Notices were published for the M100 Contracts on 19th May 2025: • Civils Enabling Works Framework TED Reference: 320539-2025 - Planning • Utilities Framework TED Reference: 319450-2025 - Planning • Enabling Works and Specialist Heritage Works Framework TED Reference: 321121-2025 - Planning • Independent Monitoring and Surveying Qualification System TED Reference: 321586-2025 - Planning • Archaeology Services Qualification System TED Reference: 321984-2025 - Planning This Global PIN is further to other previous publications concerning this project including: • TED Reference: 518372-2024, released on 29 of August 2024, related to the M400 Main Civils Infrastructure Contracts. • TED Reference: 509146-2024, released on 26 August 2024, related to the PDP Contract. • TED Reference: 557522-2023, released on 15 September 2023, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 208843-2022, released on 19 April 2022, related to the M500 Contract. • TED Reference: 536230-2019, released on 12 November 2019, related to MetroLink as a whole.

title: La réalisation de l'évaluation globale du Contrat vert et bleu du Grand Rovaltain porté par le Syndicat Mixte du SCoT Rovaltain Drôme Ardèche
description: La réalisation de l'évaluation globale du Contrat vert et bleu du Grand Rovaltain porté par le Syndicat Mixte du SCoT Rovaltain Drôme Ardèche | BP 15191 | 26958 | VALENCE Cedex 9 | Le Contrat vert et bleu du Grand Rovaltain s'étend sur la période 2015-2021, avec l'appui de la Région Auvergne Rhône Alpes, de l'Europe (FEDER), de l'Agence de l'Eau Rhône Méditerranée Corse, et des Départements de la Drôme et de l'Ardèche, et en partenariat technique et scientifique avec le Conservatoire des espaces naturels Rhône Alpes.Les 58 actions inscrites au Contrat vert et bleu portent sur l'ensemble des milieux naturels du Grand Rovaltain : les zones humides, les pelouses sèches, les cours d'eau, les milieux forestiers et agricoles.Les porteurs d'actions sont au nombre de 20, représentant une grande diversité des acteurs agissant en faveur des continuités écologiques du territoire : associations, partenaires privés, collectivitésLa présente mission a pour objet la réalisation de l'évaluation globale du Contrat vert et bleu du Grand Rovaltain.Dans un premier temps, le référentiel des indicateurs d'évaluation devra être consolidé sur la base de la version déjà réalisée (CEN RA/SM SCoT), construit à partir de six questions évaluatives (Phase 1 - Etape 1).Suite à cette étape, l'ensemble des indicateurs devra être récolté, ainsi que tout élément nécessaire à l'évaluation, auprès des différents acteurs concernés (Phase 1 - Etape 2).A partir de ces valeurs d'indicateurs, une analyse devra être proposée aboutissant à un jugement évaluatif du Contrat vert et bleu. La méthode d'analyse sera à proposer par le prestataire (Phase 2). De plus, l'évaluation du contrat devra contenir un volet sociologique et un volet géomatique.Enfin, des perspectives et des pistes d'amélioration devront être tracées. On insistera sur la première partie, qui consistera à déterminer les enjeux " résolus " et " persistants " suite à la réalisation du CVB, sur la base d'une mise à jour cartographique de l'état des lieux de la trame écologique du Grand Rovaltain (Phase 3 - Partie 1).En fin de mission, un support de communication sera a réaliser | 9

title: INTER SATELLITE LINK V-BAND SOLID STATE POWER AMPLIFIER MODULE (ARTES AT 5C.381)
description: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test an enabling inter satellite link V- Band solid state power amplifier module breadboard delivering 10W saturated power with better than 15% efficiency for Intersatellite RF links of at least 10Gbps over a distance of 1000 km.Targeted Improvements:Enabling technology development for RF Intersatellite links achieving 10Gbps and beyond in the 1000 km distance range.Description:Future NGSO constellations, GSO relay satellites relay and also multiple access telecom reconfigurable satellite systems require high data-rate inter-satellite-links (ISL) to overcome feeder link capacity saturation.RF ISL have been demonstrated more than 20 years ago and current ISL achieve 1-2 Gb/s per channel. Higher data rates are achieved with optical ISL such as on EDRS with up to 1.8Gb/s over long distances and 5.625Gb/s over short distances. An alternative or complementary solution is RF data links using a very high frequency band where significant bandwidth is available (59 to 71 GHz). More than10Gb/s is feasible for distances of up to at least 5000km and even higher data rates for short distances.In order to enable RF ISLat10 Gb/s and above, this activity will design and develop the critical technology: a V-Band solid state high power amplifier (SSPA) module. A concept for the RF output section of the ISL shall be selected and a breadboard of a 10 W V-Band SSPA module shall be manufactured and tested with a power added efficiency of at least 15%.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl.
